items.title: Attackers Actively Probing for Upgrade-Window RCE Vulnerability in WordPress Core
items.summary:
On October 28th, 2026, the WordPress Security Team released WordPress 7.1.4, along with backported security releases for older branches, addressing several security issues, most notably an Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability in WordPress core, identified as CVE-2026-119977. The vulnerability affects WordPress core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 and can be leveraged by unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during a core upgrade, which can lead to complete site compromise.

items.title: HTTP2Shell: What the Critical Brotli Vulnerability Means for WordPress Sites
items.summary:
On October 22, 2026, Google published CVE-2026-111497, a critical vulnerability in Brotli, one day after the Brotli project released fixed versions. The vulnerability has circulated under several unofficial names, including HTTP2Shell, Node2Shell, and Brotli2Shell.

The post HTTP2Shell: What the Critical Brotli Vulnerability Means for WordPress Sites appeared first on Wordfence.

items.title: WordPress 7.1.4 Patches Unauthenticated Upgrade-Window RCE; Exploitation Attempts Detected After Release
items.summary:
WordPress 7.1.4 was released on October 28, 2026. According to WordPress, it includes fixes for 22 security vulnerabilities. The most serious is an unauthenticated race condition in the Core update process that can lead to remote code execution. Threat actors are already actively attempting to exploit it, so site owners should verify that WordPress has updated to 7.1.4 or the corresponding security release for their branch.
